youtube.title: How Much House Can You Really Afford? ($60K, $100K, $150K)
youtube.description:
How much house can you really afford on a $60K, $100K or $150K salary? Your mortgage approval is not your budget. Here's the 28/36 rule worked out with this week's mortgage rate, plus the hidden costs of buying a home most calculators skip.

Numbers in this video
• 30-year fixed mortgage rate: 7.28% average as of Nov 19, 2026; 6.26% a year earlier (Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey)
• Lenders: Fannie Mae allows a debt-to-income ratio up to 50% for loans run through Desktop Underwriter (Fannie Mae Selling Guide B3-6-02)
• 28/36 rule: housing (principal, interest, taxes, insurance) under 28% of gross income; all debts under 36%. A guideline, not a law.
• Median existing-home price: $416,700 in October 2026; first-time buyers were 29% of sales (National Association of Realtors)
• Our examples assume 10% down, a 30-year fixed loan at 7.28%, and property taxes + insurance of about 1.5% of the price per year. Results: about $189K (on $60K), $315K ($100K), $472K ($150K) at 28%, vs about $337K, $562K and $844K at a 50% debt ratio with no other debts. Estimates only; your taxes, insurance, PMI and rate will differ.
• Maintenance of 1–2% of the home's value per year is a common rule of thumb.

Watch next: The #1 Wealth Killer No One Talks About: Lifestyle Creep.

Which income is closest to yours, and what did your bank approve you for? Tell me in the comments.
